meta.title: Ascend-H3 | Efficient generation on Ascend
meta.description: Ascend-H3 brings MiniMax H3 audio-video generation inference to Ascend NPUs.

labels.hero: GO THERE LAB / OPEN SOURCE INFERENCE
labels.footer: AN OPEN INFERENCE PROJECT BY GO THERE LAB

hero.headline: Beyond model migration: deeper into domestic compute.
hero.description1: Designing video-generation attention paths for Ascend NPUs.
hero.description2: From sparse operators and quantization to multi-device inference.

overview.intro: Around MiniMax H3, we go beyond deploying a model on Ascend NPUs to design attention execution paths for video generation on a domestic compute platform.
overview.body1: Many efficient attention methods were originally built around the GPU ecosystem. Running them on Ascend requires more than loading a model: blocks, routing, data layouts and low-level computation must be organized for the hardware. Ascend-H3 integrates Full, VSA, Veda, VDN and Spark-H3 in one inference framework, spanning attention computation through audio-video generation.
overview.body2: The project builds on vLLM-Omni model loading and serving, with INT8 linear-layer quantization, multi-device TP / SP and VAE decoding. The current integration targets batch-one text-to-audio-video generation (T2VA) without reference video.
overview.execution: Block selection, data permutation and on-chip computation adapt different attention methods to NPU execution.
overview.precision: Linear layers use native W8A8 INT8; projection outputs enter attention as BF16. Required predictor, accumulation and state operations retain FP32.
overview.generation: From text encoding and DiT denoising to audio-video decoding and MP4 output, the project supports validated 768p workloads.

methods.intro: Starting with full attention as a baseline, the implementation adapts sparse routing, data permutation, dual branches and hierarchical partitioning.

full.label: FULL ATTENTION / BASELINE
full.description: CANN fused attention performs the full computation, providing a same-device, same-shape baseline for the sparse paths. Model loading and projections are managed by the vLLM-Omni inference stack.
full.note: Full-attention baseline; explicit masks in auxiliary token refiners use the upstream masked SDPA path.

vsa.label: VIDEO SPARSE ATTENTION / ROUTING
vsa.description: Video tokens are arranged into logical 4×4×4 blocks, and pooled routing selects the regions to compute. The Ascend operator pairs selected logical KV64 blocks into on-chip KV128 compute tiles.
vsa.note: Loads the complete official FastH3 V2 student and trained gates. Invalid boundary tokens remain masked, while text and audio prefixes retain dense attention.

veda.label: DYNAMIC ROUTING / BLOCK SELECTION
veda.description: A pretrained per-layer, per-head predictor recomputes routes for every attention call. Tokens are permuted by selected blocks, processed by sparse softmax, then restored to their original order.
veda.note: Tensor parallelism shards local data heads while the predictor retains global head IDs. Default nominal video sparsity is 90%.

vdn.label: LINEAR + LOCAL / DUAL BRANCH
vdn.description: The learned DeltaNet linear branch and local softmax branch are retained. The linear branch uses a centered Newton iteration for approximate matrix inversion, while bidirectional scans reduce host dispatch overhead.
pipeline: Local softmax ∥ DeltaNet (approximate inverse and bidirectional scans)
vdn.note: All 128 state dimensions are retained by default. Newton inversion is a numerical approximation and is not claimed to be bitwise identical to Cholesky or triangular solves.

spark.label: HIERARCHICAL SPARSITY / PARTITIONING
spark.description: Content-dependent routing uses hierarchical balanced token partitions: selected blocks contribute original K/V, while unselected blocks contribute proxy K/V. A shared online softmax normalizes them jointly.
spark.note: The proxy branch includes mass correction, and the dense prefix participates in the same normalization. Default nominal sparsity of the exact branch is 90%.

chart.explainer: End-to-end latency for five methods; shorter bars are faster. Single- and 8-NPU charts share a scale for the same frame count; 124- and 345-frame scales differ.
chart.offloadComparison: For single-NPU 345-frame runs, VSA, VDN and Spark use layerwise offload, while Full and Veda use text-only offload; 8-NPU SP uses no runtime offload. Differences in latency cannot be attributed solely to the method or parallel efficiency.

performance.intro: Cross-device core comparisons and Ascend end-to-end measurements distinguish relative operator speedups, absolute latency and multi-device scaling.
performance.coreIntro: In some tests, the Ascend sparse method's speedup over its own Full baseline matches or exceeds the corresponding RTX PRO 6000 (Blackwell) speedup.
performance.coreWarning: This does not mean lower absolute latency across devices.
performance.coreNote: 1344×768, 124 / 345 frames; BF16 main weights and activations, with weights resident on both devices. Frozen synthetic hidden states and real student weights are used for three measurements each at layers 0, 24 and 49, averaged over nine runs. Speedup uses the Full core on the same device and shape as its baseline; it is not a direct speed ratio between devices. Absolute latencies are shown too. Timing starts with prepared Q/K/V and ends at the attention output. It includes required gates, prediction, block selection, permutation and both VDN branches; it excludes QKV projection, Q/K norm, RoPE, output projection, AdaLN and FFN. It is not end-to-end latency.
performance.e2eNote: 1344×768, eight actual DiT updates, seed 7. Timing includes text encoding, audio-video decoding and MP4 output, but excludes model loading and warmup. †T: text-encoder offload; †L: layerwise DiT / text offload. Offload policies may differ between single- and multi-device runs, so speedup is not pure parallel efficiency.
performance.e2eSource: View complete TP / SP results and protocol

videos.intro: Ascend 910B3, 1344×768, 124 frames at 24 FPS (about 5.17 seconds), with audio. Each method uses the same prompt, offload policy and eight forwards.
videos.note: Videos come from the project's GitHub attachments and have been checked against the recorded SHA256 hashes. These samples support inspection, not a claim of quality improvement on their own.
